title: Government Intervention Adventure 2: Price Controls
welcome_lead: Today you'll set a price ceiling and a price floor — and see who wins or loses.
meta_desc: Economics: price ceilings (max price) and price floors (min price), shortages and surpluses.
final_note: You analysed price ceilings and floors and their welfare consequences.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A ceiling below equilibrium produces a shortage.

Quantity supplied falls; consumers want more; rationing by queue, lottery, or favouritism. Black markets emerge.

Examples: rent control, pandemic price gouging laws.

A floor above equilibrium produces a surplus.

Examples: minimum wage (labour surplus = unemployment if floor bites), agricultural price support (EU CAP butter mountains).

Government may need to buy the surplus, sell it abroad, or destroy it.

Ceilings help poor consumers but create shortages and queues.

Floors protect producers/workers but cause surplus and unemployment.

Both reduce total surplus and create deadweight loss vs the free market — but may improve equity.
